Three things you are always responsible for when using a cloud provider?
column3: info and data stores; devices allowed to connect; accounts and identities of people/services/devices in your org.

column1: Three things the cloud provider is always responsible for?
column3: physical security; network infrastructure; host hardware and virtualization layer.

column1: a set of (Microsoft) technologies that helps manage your cloud environment
column3: whether it's a public cloud solely on Azure; a private cloud in your datacenter; a hybrid configuration; or even a multi-cloud environment

column1: A new building; repaving the parking lot; building a datacenter; or buying a company vehicle are examples of:
column3: CapEx is typically a one-time; up-front expenditure to purchase or secure tangible resources.

column1: Renting a convention center; leasing a company vehicle; or signing up for cloud services are all examples of:
column3: OpEx is spending money on services or products over time.

column1: Adding more CPU's or RAM to a virtual machine is an example of:
column3: vertical scaling (or scaling up) means increasing or decreasing the capabilities of resources

column1: Adding additional virtual machines or containers is an example of:
column3: horizontal scaling (or scaling out) means adding (or subtracting) more instances of resources

column1: Two types of predictability in MS Azure Well-Architechted Framework ?/?
column3: Performance predictability ensures that your applications consistently meet performance requirements under varying loads; Cost predictability helps you manage and forecast your cloud expenses effectively.

column1: Term for feature that can deploy additional resources to meet the demand
column3: Autoscaling automatically adjusts the number of active servers or resources based on current demand; ensuring optimal performance and cost-efficiency.

column1: Feature of the cloud to help better plan resource deployments
column3: Data analytics tools can analyze historical usage patterns and predict future resource needs; helping organizations optimize their cloud deployments.

column1: Two tools they list to better estimate cost of potential cloud spend? (acronym/full name)
column3: The Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) Calculator helps estimate the cost savings of migrating to Azure; The Pricing Calculator allows you to estimate the cost of Azure services based on your projected usage.

column1: The main type of template that ensures all deployed resources meet standards/requirements
column3: ARM templates are JSON files that define the infrastructure and configuration for your Azure solution; (Bicep is a newer; friendlier language that compiles down to ARM templates)

column1: What feature looks for and flags resources that are out of compliance?
column3: Auditing continuously monitors your resources to ensure they comply with organizational policies and standards; flagging any deviations for review and remediation.

column1: Term for framework of policies/controls that ensure cloud resources are used properly & in compliance?
column3: Governance encompasses the policies; processes; and controls that ensure effective and compliant use of cloud resources within an organization.

column1: Three things where responsibility can vary with PaaS (???/???/???)
column3: networking settings and connectivity within your cloud environment; network and application security; and the directory infrastructure.

column1: Two uses of PaaS besides a Dev Framework?
column3: Business Intelligence (BI) tools help organizations analyze data and make informed decisions; Analytics platforms provide tools for data analysis; visualization; and reporting.

column1: Microsoft's cloud based ID & Access management services new name
column3: formerly Azure Active Directory (Azure AD); Entra ID provides identity and access management services for cloud-based applications and resources.

column1: For business and enterprise users; Microsoft 365 operates as a ? ? service
column3: This means while Microsoft manages the infrastructure; your organization controls how services are configured and used.

column1: What did Office 365 evolve from?
column3: Business Productivity Online Suite (BPOS) was the predecessor to Office 365; it provided hosted versions of Microsoft Exchange; SharePoint; and Lync services.

column1: Microsofts platform that includes Intune and EntraID (Acronym)
column3: Enterprise Mobility + Security (EMS) is a suite of tools that includes Intune for device management and Entra ID for identity and access management.

column1: Two intelligent tools built into Word 365 ?/?
column3: Editor provides advanced grammar and style suggestions to improve writing quality; Researcher helps users find credible sources and content for their documents.

column1: How copilot in Excel can help?
column3: They specifically say 'insights; trends and visualizations' from your data.

column1: Two intelligent tools in PowerPoint 365 ?/?
column3: Designer suggests design layouts and visual enhancements for slides; Speaker Coach provides feedback on presentation delivery; including pacing; tone; and use of filler words.

column1: How Copilot in OneNote can help (generally) ?/?
column3: Copilot can help summarize notes; organize content; and generate ideas for better note-taking.

column1: Copilot in OneNote can also help by creating ?/?
column3: Copilot can assist in creating lists; plans; and action items based on your notes.

column1: The main thing they say Copilot does in Outlook besides writing stuff?
column3: Copilot can help summarize lengthy email threads; highlight key points; and suggest responses.

column1: View types in MS Project? (the weird named two) ?/?
column3: Kanban view provides a visual way to manage tasks using boards and cards; Gantt view displays tasks along a timeline; showing dependencies and progress.

column1: Microsoft Project is built on the ?
column3: Microsoft Project leverages the Power Platform to enhance project management capabilities; including automation; data analysis; and custom app development.

column1: Three key elements of Microsoft Loop ?/?/?
column3: Components are individual units of content that can be shared and collaborated on; Pages are flexible canvases that organize components and content; Workspaces are collaborative environments where teams can work together on projects and ideas.

column1: A smart information tracking app to organize information and work?
column3: Microsoft Lists helps users track information; organize work; and collaborate with team members through customizable lists and views. Track item history with versions.

column1: What is the app for scheduling meetings and stuff called?
column3: Microsoft Bookings is an online scheduling tool that allows businesses to manage appointments; bookings; and customer interactions efficiently.

column1: Provides a simple and visual way for teams to organize their work; task-based initiatives
column3: Microsoft Planner enables teams to create; assign; and track tasks using visual boards; making it easy to manage projects and collaborate effectively.
